1.w: Now concerning the [things] of which you⁺ wrote: [It is] good for a man not to touch a woman.

2.w: But because of the sexual immorality, let each man have his [own] wife, and let each woman have [her] own husband.

3.w: Let the husband render the duty to the wife, and likewise also the wife to the husband.

4.w: The wife does not have authority over [her] own body, but the husband; and likewise also, the husband does not have authority over [his] own body, but the wife.

5.w: Do not deprive one another, except by mutual agreement for a time, so that you⁺ might be at leisure for prayer, and may be together the same again, so that Satan may not tempt you⁺ through your⁺ lack of self-control.

6.w: Now I say this by way of concession, not by way of command.

7.w: Yet I wish all men to be even like myself. But each has his own gift from God; indeed the one thus, but the one thus.

8.w: Now I say to the unmarried and to the widows: [It is] good for them if they should remain as even I [am].

9.w: But if they do not have self-control, let them marry, for it is better to marry than to burn.

10.w: Now to those having married I command (not I, but the Lord): A wife is not to be separated from a husband.

11.w: But if indeed she might be separated, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to the husband; and a husband is not to send away a wife.

12.w: Now to the rest I say (I, not the Lord): If any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she consents to dwell with him, let him not send her away.

13.w: And if any woman has an unbelieving husband, and he consents to dwell with her, let her not send away the husband.

14.w: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the brother. Otherwise, then your⁺ children are unclean; but now they are holy.

15.w: But if the unbeliever separates himself, let him separate himself. The brother or the sister is not bound in such [cases]. But God has called you⁺ in peace.

16.w: For how do you know, wife, if you will save the husband? Or how do you know, husband, if you will save the wife?

17.w: Nevertheless, as the Lord apportioned to each, as God has called each, thus let him walk. And thus I direct in all the churches.

18.w: Was anyone called having been circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.

19.w: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping of the commandments of God.

20.w: Each in the calling in which he has been called—in this let him remain.

21.w: Were you called [while] a slave? Let it not be a care to you; but if also you have power to become free, rather use [it].

22.w: For the one having been called in the Lord [while] a slave is the Lord’s freedman; likewise the one having been called [while] free is a slave of Christ.

23.w: You⁺ were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men.

24.w: Each in that in which he was called, brothers—in this let him remain with God.

25.w: Now concerning the virgins, I do not have a commandment of the Lord, but I give judgment as one having received mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.

26.w: Therefore I think this is good, because of the present necessity, that [it is] good for a man to be thus.

27.w: Have you been bound to a wife? Do not seek to be loosed. Have you been loosed from a wife? Do not seek a wife.

28.w: But if also you shall have married, you did not sin; and if the virgin shall have married, she did not sin. But such will have tribulation in the flesh, and I am sparing you⁺.

29.w: Now I say this, brothers: The time is shortened—so that from now on both those having wives should be as not having;

30.w: and those weeping, as not weeping; and those rejoicing, as not rejoicing; and those buying, as not possessing;

31.w: and those using the world, as not using [it] up. For the form of this world is passing away.

32.w: But I want you⁺ to be without concern. The unmarried man is concerned for the [things] of the Lord, how he should please the Lord;

33.w: but the one being married is concerned for the [things] of the world, how he should please the wife,

34.w: and is divided. And the unmarried woman and virgin is concerned for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit; but the one being married is concerned for the things of the world, how she should please the husband.

35.w: Now I say this for your⁺ own profit, not so that I might place upon you⁺ a restraint, but for what [is] seemly and devoted to the Lord, without distraction.

36.w: But if anyone supposes [himself] to be acting unbecomingly to his virgin, if she is beyond youth, and it ought to be so, let him do what he wills; he does not sin; let them marry.

37.w: But he who has stood steadfast in his heart, not having necessity but having authority over [his] own will, and has judged this in [his] own heart, to keep his own virgin, he will do well.

38.w: So then also, the one marrying [his] own virgin does well, and the one not marrying will do better.

39.w: A wife has been bound for as long a time [as] her husband may live; but if the husband shall have died, she is free to be married to whom she wants, only in the Lord.

40.w: But she is more blessed if she should remain in the same manner, according to my judgment; and I think myself also to have the Spirit of God.
